title: Size of the Recursive Bribery Set
statement: Let $n\ge 2$, and let $f$ be a monotone Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$ with positive bias. Let $a<1$ be a real target and let $t\le n$. Starting from the empty set, form the recursively selected bribery set by adjoining a maximum-influence coordinate whenever setting the coordinates already selected to $+1$ leaves the mean of the resulting function below $a$, and otherwise leaving the set unchanged. If, after $t$ steps, that mean is still below $a$, then the selected set has cardinality exactly $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$
The positive bias of $f$ is positive
$t$ is a natural number with $t\le n$
After bribing the recursively selected set at step $t$ to $+1$, the mean is below $a$
